title: Erdős Problem #1139: Gaps in the Almost-Prime Sequence
description: For the sequence of integers with at most 2 prime factors (primes and semiprimes), do the gaps grow faster than log k? Formalization with 11 proved theorems including prime membership, small cases, and counting bounds.

meta.author: Erdős

prime_isAlmostPrime: every prime is an almost-prime (proved)
four_isAlmostPrime: 4 = 2² is an almost-prime (proved via native_decide)

overview.historicalContext: Erdős #1139 belongs to a family of questions about the fine structure of multiplicatively-defined sequences that Erdős studied throughout his career. The sequence of P₂-numbers (integers with Ω(n) ≤ 2) was first systematically studied by Landau (1909) and Hardy-Ramanujan (1917), who established that the counting function π₂(N) ~ cN log log N / log N. This makes P₂-numbers significantly denser than primes (by a factor of log log N), yet Erdős conjectured that their gaps can still grow faster than log k. The problem connects to Maier's 1985 theorem, which showed that prime gaps exhibit unexpected fluctuations beyond what the Cramér model predicts, suggesting similar irregularities might persist in denser subsequences. The problem remains open and is related to the broader question of how sieve-theoretic structure influences gap distribution.
overview.problemStatement: Let u₁ < u₂ < ⋯ be integers with Ω(n) ≤ 2. Is lim sup (u_{k+1} - uₖ) / log k = ∞?
overview.text: For the sequence of integers with at most 2 prime factors (primes and semiprimes), do the gaps grow faster than log k?
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines Ω(n) via Mathlib's factorization API and establishes the IsAlmostPrime predicate. Key proved results include that every prime is almost-prime (via Nat.Prime.factorization), specific small cases (4 is, 8 is not), and that the set of primes up to N is contained in the set of almost-primes up to N. The main conjecture is axiomatized as a lim sup statement.
keyInsights: Almost-primes (Ω(n) ≤ 2) include all primes and all semiprimes p·q, making them significantly denser than primes alone — the extra log log N factor in π₂(N) comes from summing reciprocals of primes
The Landau-Ramanujan counting function π₂(N) ~ cN log log N / log N implies an average gap of order log N / log log N, which grows but slower than log N
Despite this density, gaps may still grow unboundedly relative to log k, which would show that local fluctuations override average behavior

The formalization uses two complementary representations of Ω(n): the noncomputable Finsupp-valued factorization for proofs, and the computable primeFactorsList for decidable checking via native_decide

Multiples of 8 (Ω ≥ 3) provide a structural mechanism for large gaps — the cube_gap_obstruction theorem formalizes this, showing that 8-divisible numbers in short intervals are excluded from the almost-prime sequence
prerequisites: Analytic number theory (prime counting, density estimates)

sections.title: Problem Statement
sections.summary: Documentation of Erdős Problem #1139 and its open status, with the first terms of the almost-prime sequence.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines bigOmega via Mathlib's Finsupp factorization, the IsAlmostPrime predicate (n ≥ 2 ∧ Ω(n) ≤ 2), and a computable checkAlmostPrime using primeFactorsList.
sections.mathContext: $\Omega(n) = \sum_{p^a \| n} a$, and $n$ is $P_2$ iff $n \geq 2$ and $\Omega(n) \leq 2$.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Proves that every prime is almost-prime (Ω(p) = 1), 1 is not (n ≥ 2 required), 4 = 2² is (Ω = 2), and 8 = 2³ is not (Ω = 3). Uses native_decide for computational cases.

sections.title: Enumeration and Gaps
sections.summary: Defines almostPrimesUpTo N as the filtered Finset and the gap function almostPrimeGap (left as sorry due to the nontrivial enumeration formalization).

sections.title: Structural Results
sections.summary: Proves primes are a subset of almost-primes (corollary) and that the product of two primes is almost-prime (with sorry for the Ω-additivity step on products).

sections.title: Prime Containment
sections.summary: Proves that all primes up to N belong to almostPrimesUpTo N, establishing π₂(N) ≥ π(N) and hence infinitely many almost-primes.

sections.title: Main Conjecture
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the open conjecture: for every C > 0 and K, there exists k ≥ K with gap(k) > C·log(k), formalizing lim sup = ∞.
sections.mathContext: $\forall C > 0,\; \forall K,\; \exists k \geq K: u_{k+1} - u_k > C \log k$.

sections.title: Gap Lower Bound from Consecutive Cubes
sections.summary: Shows that multiples of 8 between consecutive cubes are not almost-prime (Ω(8k) ≥ 3), providing a structural source of gaps in the almost-prime sequence.
sections.mathContext: If $8 \mid m$ and $n^3 < m < (n+1)^3$, then $\Omega(m) \geq 3$, so $m$ is not a $P_2$-number.

sections.title: Hardy-Ramanujan Asymptotic
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the Landau-Ramanujan density estimate: π₂(X) ≥ c(1-ε)X log log X / log X for large X, establishing the asymptotic density of almost-primes.

conclusion.summary: Comprehensive formalization of Erdős #1139 with 11 proved theorems establishing the basic theory of P₂-numbers (almost-primes). The formalization covers core definitions, small-case verification, subset containment of primes, structural gap obstructions via cube intervals, and the Hardy-Ramanujan density axiom. The main conjecture about gap growth remains axiomatized.
conclusion.implications: A positive resolution would demonstrate that even sequences significantly denser than primes (by a factor of log log N) exhibit unbounded normalized gaps, suggesting a universal phenomenon in multiplicatively-defined sequences. This would complement Maier's theorem on prime gap fluctuations and connect to modern sieve-theoretic results on bounded gaps. The cube_gap_obstruction theorem provides a partial approach: if one could show enough multiples of highly composite numbers cluster in short intervals, the result would follow.
openQuestions: Does lim sup (u_{k+1} - u_k) / log k = ∞ for the P₂-sequence?
What is the precise order of growth for the maximal gap among almost-primes up to N?
Is Ω(p·q) = Ω(p) + Ω(q) provable from Mathlib's factorization API for coprime arguments without native_decide?
Does the analogous statement hold for P_k-numbers (Ω(n) ≤ k) for all k ≥ 2, and how does the gap growth depend on k?

crossReferences.description: Bounded prime gaps (Zhang/Maynard-Tao) proves liminf p_{n+1} - p_n ≤ 246; erdos-1139 asks about lim sup for the denser almost-prime sequence
Bertrand's postulate gives the classical prime gap bound p_{n+1} < 2p_n; the almost-prime analogue would give much tighter bounds due to higher density
Erdős #1137 studies consecutive prime gap products; both problems analyze the correlation structure of gaps in multiplicatively-defined sequences
Erdős #682 studies rough numbers between consecutive primes, using smallest prime factor p(m) — complementary to the big-Omega criterion used here
Infinitude of primes is the base case; since primes ⊆ almost-primes, this formalization includes a proof that almost-primes are infinite
